Notes. This review is for operators who must judge credential and quota health at a glance.

The product now reads as a competent professional dashboard. Its shell and mobile re-layout are measured strengths from the screenshots.

It is not yet at excellent craft. The blockers are separable quota data, competing refresh controls, low-contrast secondary text, and desktop-only affordance gaps named above.

Every score below 9.0 in this round is tied to a concrete observed issue in its metric evidence.

**Notes.**

- **Overall: 7.88.** The product reads as a competent, restrained ops console. The gap to 9 is consistency and use of known state, not new visual direction. Each of the top fixes is visible on more than one screen.
- **Fixture data versus defects.** Several features come from the fixture data, not the design: the uniform 62% quota, 0 dashboard requests, the empty plugin registry, and "Daily … Not reported". I did not score these as defects. The quota and usage findings are about what the design shows (axes, labels, color coding, KPI composition), not about sparse data.
- **Source checks.** I read source only to settle two points. The Proxy URL text is a placeholder (`sharedFields.tsx:61`). Placeholder color uses `--text-tertiary` (`reset.scss:43`). I calculated the contrast ratios from the theme tokens and did not measure them from pixels.
- **Mobbin.** No Mobbin references were checked. I compared against general developer-dashboard conventions only.
